question: Can the exact full-aperture phase-variance objective keep the blocked fftA intermediate on-chip (served from GPU cache instead of device memory) by shrinking the per-dispatch working set without multiplying kernel drains, i.e. by fusing column-pass(batch k) and row-pass(batch k-1) into one dispatch, and does that measurably beat the retained blocked-4 schedule (best 221.6 ms p50, same-session repeats 222-257 ms) with bit-identical object, loss, and optimizer trajectory?

code.diff_scope: git diff -- src at experiment start (includes the accepted blocked-4 fftA layout from 20260911-ssb-fft-intermediate, uncommitted)
code.prototype_archive: pipelined-prototype.patch (apply with git apply --unidiff-zero; not production-qualified)
code.publication_note: Unfinished persistent scheduler preserved as a patch, excluded from production source pending exactness and performance qualification.
code.note: Starting point is the accepted blocked 4-row fftA schedule (phase batch 8, two encoders per batch, one command buffer per objective). Candidate patches are recorded per arm; rejected code is removed.

parameters.precision: complex64/float32; exact packed original uint32 counts
parameters.scope: Kernel-level real-data A/B on the reference-512 original file via ssb-scheduling-probe; compare.py against an adjacent same-session baseline. Not synthetic evidence, not a UI frame rate.
plan: baseline: blocked-4 production schedule, this session
preliminary: production kernels at phase batch 4/2/1 (isolated, one constant), to separate dispatch-drain cost from cache residency
microbenchmark: write X MB then read X MB in adjacent dispatches for X in 1..64 MB, to size the on-chip write->read retention
candidate: fused-role dispatch (column pass batch k + row pass batch k-1, double-buffered fftA) at the batch size the microbenchmark supports
parameters.design_decision: Serial-dispatch schemes cannot win: batch-1 dispatches are latency-bound (~26/22 us per BF vs 18.4/8.9 us at batch 8), so any topology with a <=2 MB live intermediate needs the row pass to consume inside the same dispatch. Candidate: persistent work-queue kernel; W worker groups (256 threads) claim items in fixed order [COL(8k+0)x65][COL(8k+1)x65][ROW(k)x64][COL(8k+2..7)x65...]; COL item = 4 columns of one BF (exact pass-1 code, blocked store into ring slot bf % S); ROW item = 2 row blocks x up to 8 BFs (exact pass-2 tile/mirror/IFFT/phase code, 8-BF register sums, phase_sum += sum serialized per row-block pair by a batch counter). Counters: col_done[bf] (65), row_done[bf] (64), flush_done[rbp]; fences via atomic_thread_fence(device). Deadlock-freedom: only one batch's 64 ROW items can wait on later-claimed COL items, so W >= 65 suffices; bounded spins set an error flag and the host falls back to the retained schedule.

execution.gpu_model: Apple M5 10-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory

outputs.result: Same-session blocked-4 production baseline: loss p50 229.89 ms, p95 232.87 ms, min 224.61 ms; object p50 75.06 ms; 12,574,949,376 B allocated; losses 0.147189587/0.146274567/0.136068195 (identical to prior session).

outputs.publication_note: Memory labels spelled out for the publication gate; measured numbers unchanged.
outputs.result: M5 write->read retention microbenchmark (3 GiB stream; per batch: stream X, write slot X, read slot X): read-only floor 26.9 ms (119.6 GB/s). Split (2 dispatches/batch) vs fused (1 dispatch/batch) p50: X=0.5 MB 39.6/33.6 ms; 1 MB 41.1/45.5; 2 MB 45.2/45.9; 4 MB 52.6/52.5; 6 MB 61.9/70.4; >=8 MB 68-76 ms (all-device memory, equals production batch 8 at 8.4 MB). Round trip is cache-served only when the live intermediate is about <=1-2 MB; 12,288 trivial dispatches cost <13 ms, so batch-1 production slowness is group latency, not fixed dispatch cost.

Concurrent residency (whole groups kept alive, trivial register use): 120 groups x 256 threads or 480 x 64 = 30,720 threads regardless of threadgroup memory 1-27 KB (about 3,072 threads/core). A first variant letting 255 threads exit reported 640 groups and was discarded as measuring one SIMD group per group.

Runtime MSL probe on macOS 26 / M5: relaxed device atomics, atomic_thread_fence(mem_device, seq_cst, thread_scope_device), volatile device loads and threadgroup_barrier(mem_device) compile; memory_order_acquire/acq_rel do not exist.
